instruction.text: Build the definition of a supply chain.

feedback.finish: Supply chains exist all around the world and involve millions of people, machines and vehicles.

atoms.b: Manufactured goods are made using raw materials such as metal, wood or cotton. These materials have to be grown or found and then ((destroyed ++harvested)).
These materials are then sent to factories to be turned into goods. This process is known as ((++manufacturing eating)).
Once they have been produced, goods are moved along global ((++supply supple)) chains using different types of transport.
They are transported and ((++stored bored)) in places such as warehouses.
The final stage of the supply chain is the retail market, where they are made available for customers to ((++buy sell)).

instruction.text: Let’s recreate a supply chain for a pair of jeans. Drag the images to where they can be found on the map.

hint.text: Most goods are made by combining materials and other products from lots of different countries.
hint.label: Did you know?

feedback.finish: In this first stage, zips are made in India, the buttons come from China, and cotton is grown and processed in Peru.

instruction.text: Drag the image to where it can be found on the map.

feedback.finish: The materials are all sent to Turkey, where they are made into jeans.

instruction.text: Drag the image to where it can be found on the map.

feedback.finish: The finished product is then sent to the UK, where it is sold in shops.

atoms.a: Many goods are made by combining materials from different countries.
A supply chain is the journey of goods being manufactured, transported and sold.
Supply chains don’t exist on an international level.
The final stage of a supply chain is the retail market, where goods are sold.
